meta.name: Birote Salado
meta.total_time: ~20 hrs (30 min active, 12–48 hrs levain ferment)
meta.description: Guadalajara's 160-year-old sourdough bread — the only culture in the Puratos World Sourdough Library fed with beer, lime juice, and egg. Shattering crust, sour-salty-bitter flavor, engineered to survive drowning in salsa for tortas ahogadas. Texas-adapted with water treatment and fermentation compensation.

change_log.summary: Feedback session: replaced lava rock steam method with dutch oven (sheet pan alternative). Added salt-in-levain rationale note to BUILD_LEVAIN with source citations.
Initial recipe from multi-agent research synthesis (7 agents, 31 sources). Texas-adapted from Stellanspice, Breadtopia, Lesaffre Mexico, and Grupo La Florida professional formulas.

ingredients.name: Active Sourdough Starter
ingredients.rationale: 1:1 ratio with levain flour. Must be active and bubbly — doubled within 4-8 hours of last feeding.

ingredients.name: All-Purpose Flour
ingredients.rationale: Mexican flour is 9% protein — US AP flour (10-12%) is closer than bread flour. An 80/20 AP/bread blend also works for more structure.

ingredients.name: Mexican Lager Beer
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Stellanspice, Breadtopia, Grupo La Florida (7/7 agents)
ingredients.rationale: Slows fermentation via hops antimicrobial, adds malt character, creates selection pressure for T. delbrueckii yeast. Modelo Especial or Pacifico.

ingredients.name: Egg (whisked)
ingredients.rationale: ~1/2 large egg. Lecithin emulsifies, protein adds structure. Only sourdough in the Puratos collection fed with egg.

ingredients.name: Fresh Lime Juice
ingredients.rationale: Immediately acidifies the levain, supports LAB, adds citrus tang. May historically compensate for alkaline water.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.rationale: Feeds yeast, balances acidity in the hostile levain environment.

ingredients.name: Fine Sea Salt
ingredients.rationale: 2.3% of total flour. 'Salado' means salted — birote is intentionally saltier than standard bread.

ingredients.name: Filtered Water
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Professional GDL formulas (Lesaffre 63%, Grupo La Florida 62%)
ingredients.rationale: 62.5% hydration. Carbon-filtered Austin tap diluted 50/50 with distilled water to reduce hardness and alkalinity.

states.title: Mix Birote Levain
states.direction: In the medium bowl (V1), combine 80g active sourdough starter, 80g AP flour, 40g Mexican lager beer, 30g whisked egg (~1/2 large), 10g fresh lime juice, 8g sugar, and 1g salt. Stir vigorously until smooth and well combined.
states.exit_condition: Levain is smooth and homogeneous, all ingredients fully incorporated

notes.text: Beer must be at room temperature — cold beer will shock the starter culture. Any pale Mexican lager works: Modelo Especial, Pacifico, Victoria, Sol.
The levain will smell unusual — beery, limey, eggy. This is the authentic birote protocol used in Guadalajara for 160 years. Trust the process.

This is the only sourdough starter in the Puratos World Sourdough Library (#72 of 133) fed with beer, egg, and lime juice. It cultivates Torulaspora delbrueckii, a rare yeast that produces fruity esters.

The 1g salt is intentional — both Stellanspice and Breadtopia include salt in the levain build. At 0.4% of levain weight, it mildly boosts LAB activity without meaningfully inhibiting yeast (inhibition starts at 2%+). Lesaffre Mexico's professional formula includes salt in the esponja at an even higher ratio.

states.title: Cold Ferment Levain
states.direction: Cover the bowl and let the levain rise ~50% at room temperature (about 2 hours). Then transfer to the refrigerator and cold ferment for 12-48 hours. Longer cold ferment develops more sour tang.
states.exit_condition: Levain has been cold-fermented for at least 12 hours. Should be bubbly, smell tangy and beery, and have visibly risen.

notes.text: Same-day option: skip the fridge and let the levain double at room temp (~4 hours), then use immediately. You'll get less tang but it works.
At sea level in Texas, the cold retard is especially important — it develops the sour character that altitude-accelerated fermentation produces naturally in Guadalajara.

states.title: Combine Levain and Dough
states.direction: Remove levain from fridge. In the large bowl (V2), combine all levain (~250g) with 250g filtered water. Stir to dissolve and loosen. Add 400g AP flour. Mix with a rubber spatula until no dry flour remains — a shaggy, sticky mass.
states.exit_condition: All ingredients combined into a shaggy mass with no dry flour visible

notes.text: Use carbon-filtered Austin tap water diluted 50/50 with distilled. Austin's water (pH 8.82, 290 mg/L hardness) is too alkaline and hard for optimal sourdough.

states.title: Autolyse Rest
states.direction: Cover the bowl and let the dough rest for 30 minutes. The flour hydrates and gluten begins developing passively.
states.exit_condition: 30 minutes elapsed, dough is slightly smoother and more cohesive than when first mixed

states.title: Add Salt
states.direction: Sprinkle 5g salt over the dough. With wet hands, perform 4 stretch-and-folds. Sprinkle remaining 5g salt. Continue folding until salt is fully distributed — no gritty texture when you pinch the dough.
states.exit_condition: Salt fully incorporated, no gritty texture when pinching dough

states.title: Coil Fold — Set 1
states.direction: With wet hands, release the dough from the sides of the bowl. Slide hands under the center, lift the dough up and let each end fold under itself from gravity. Rotate the bowl 90° and repeat. The dough drapes over your hands and tucks under.
states.exit_condition: Dough has been coil-folded from both directions, sitting in a loose package

notes.text: Coil folds are gentler than stretch-and-folds and better for this hydration level. Wet hands prevent sticking.

states.title: Rest
states.direction: Cover the bowl and let the dough rest at room temperature for 30 minutes.
states.exit_condition: 30 minutes elapsed

states.title: Coil Fold — Set 2
states.direction: Repeat coil fold: wet hands, slide under center, lift and let ends fold under. Rotate 90°, repeat. Cover.
states.exit_condition: Dough is slightly stronger and smoother than set 1

states.title: Rest
states.direction: Cover and rest 30 minutes at room temperature.
states.exit_condition: 30 minutes elapsed

states.title: Coil Fold — Set 3
states.direction: Repeat coil fold: wet hands, slide under center, lift and let ends fold under. Rotate 90°, repeat. Cover.
states.exit_condition: Dough feels noticeably more elastic and holds its shape better

states.title: Rest
states.direction: Cover and rest 30 minutes at room temperature.
states.exit_condition: 30 minutes elapsed

states.title: Coil Fold — Set 4 (Final)
states.direction: Final coil fold: wet hands, slide under, lift, let ends fold. Rotate 90°, repeat. The dough should now be smooth, elastic, and hold its shape when folded. Cover tightly.
states.exit_condition: Dough is smooth and elastic, holds shape after folding, covered for bulk rise

states.title: Bulk Rise
states.direction: Leave covered at room temperature (75-78°F / 24-26°C) until the dough has risen ~75%. Watch for visual cues: domed surface, bubbles at top and sides, jiggles when bowl is shaken.
states.exit_condition: Dough has increased ~75% in volume, surface is domed with visible bubbles, jiggles when bowl is shaken

notes.text: At Texas sea level, expect 2-4 additional hours AFTER the coil folds (4-6 hours total bulk including folds). Guadalajara recipes claim 2 hours — that's at 5,138 ft altitude where CO2 is 17% less soluble.
Watch the dough, not the clock. The beer in the levain slows fermentation further at sea level — a double deceleration effect (higher pressure + hops).

states.title: Divide and Preshape
states.direction: Generously flour the work surface — Guadalajara bakeries use a mound of flour for shaping. Turn the dough out onto the floured surface. Using a bench scraper, divide into 5 pieces (~190g each). For each piece, pull edges to center creating tension, then flip seam-side down. Use a push-and-pull motion to tighten into a ball.
states.exit_condition: 5 roughly equal dough balls (~190g each) with light surface tension, seam-side down on floured surface

notes.text: Be generous with flour — this is a lower-hydration dough but the fermented surface can still be tacky. Watch GDL bakery videos: they work fast in a cloud of flour.

states.title: Bench Rest
states.direction: Cover the preshaped rounds with a towel and let rest on the counter for 20 minutes. The gluten relaxes, making final shaping easier.
states.exit_condition: 20 minutes elapsed, dough rounds have slightly spread but still hold general shape

states.title: Shape Torpedoes
states.direction: One at a time: gently flatten a dough round. Roll it into itself with tension, creating a tight cylinder. Pinch the seam closed. Roll into a tapered torpedo shape — fatter in the middle, pointed at both ends, about 15-18 cm long. Flour the surface after seaming. Place seam-side UP on a well-floured baker's couche or linen towel, folding the cloth between rolls for support.
states.exit_condition: 5 torpedo-shaped rolls with tapered ends, seam-up on floured couche, cloth folded between each for support

notes.text: Birote shape is NOT a baguette — it's shorter (15-18 cm / 6-7 in), fatter in the middle, with tapered ends like a football or submarine.
Flour again after seaming to prevent sticking during proof. The couche or towel should be well-floured with AP flour or rice flour.

states.title: Final Proof
states.direction: Cover the rolls on the couche and let proof at room temperature for 45-90 minutes. Use the poke test to check readiness.
states.exit_condition: Poke test: lightly flour a finger, press gently into dough — it slowly springs back about halfway. If it springs back quickly, proof longer. If it stays indented, it's over-proofed.

notes.text: Start preheating the oven 30 minutes before the rolls are ready — the baking steel and lava rocks need time to fully heat.

states.title: Preheat Oven and Steam Setup
states.direction: Place the baking steel on the upper-middle rack. Place the dutch oven (V3) with lid on the same rack or one below. Preheat to 450°F (230°C) for at least 30 minutes.
states.exit_condition: Oven at 450°F (230°C) for at least 30 minutes, baking steel and dutch oven fully preheated

notes.text: The dutch oven traps steam from the dough itself — no boiling water or wet towels needed. Preheat it with the lid on so it's ripping hot when you load the rolls.

Alternative: if you don't have a dutch oven, place a sheet pan on the lowest rack. After loading rolls on the steel, pour 1-2 cups boiling water into the sheet pan for steam. Use the oven-off method (see STEAM_REST notes) for gas ovens.

states.title: Score and Load
states.direction: Transfer proofed rolls from the couche to parchment paper. Using a bread lame, score each roll with a single slash down the center, about 1 cm deep. Spray the rolls with room-temperature water from a spray bottle. Load 2-3 rolls into the preheated dutch oven on a parchment sling. Set remaining rolls aside (covered) for the second batch.
states.exit_condition: First batch (2-3 rolls) scored, sprayed, and loaded into dutch oven with lid on. Remaining rolls covered and waiting.

notes.text: Spanish-language sources say score transversally (across, perpendicular to length). English sources say lengthwise. Both patterns exist on authentic birotes — try both and see which opens better.
Score decisively with one swift stroke. Hesitation causes dragging.

reminders.prompt: Note scoring direction used (lengthwise vs transversal)

states.title: Steam Phase — Lid On
states.direction: With the dutch oven lid on, bake at 450°F (230°C) for 20 minutes. The lid traps moisture from the dough, creating the steam environment needed for oven spring and crust development.
states.exit_condition: 20 minutes elapsed with lid on, rolls should show significant oven spring when you peek

notes.text: Do NOT open the lid during this phase — you'll release all the trapped steam. Trust the process.

Sheet pan alternative: if baking all 5 rolls on the steel at once, pour 1-2 cups boiling water into the preheated sheet pan below. For gas ovens, turn the oven OFF for this 20-minute phase — gas ovens vent steam through combustion exhaust. This 'oven off' method was the breakthrough Stellanspice discovered after 3 years of failed birote attempts.

states.title: Bake to Dark Crust
states.direction: Remove the dutch oven lid. If rolls are touching, spread them apart. Reduce oven to 425°F (220°C). Bake uncovered for 15-20 minutes until deep golden-brown. For the last 3-5 minutes, transfer rolls directly to the baking steel on the highest rack position — this develops the traditional dark, hi-bake crust that defines Guadalajara birotes. Repeat SCORE_AND_LOAD through FINISH_BAKE for the second batch.
states.exit_condition: Rolls are deep golden-brown to dark brown, internal temperature reaches 205°F (96°C), hollow sound when tapped on bottom

notes.text: Don't pull early because they look dark — the hard, dark crust is the whole point. This bread needs to survive being drowned in salsa. Pale = undercooked for birote.
Professional Guadalajara bakeries bake at 475-500°F (250°C) for 15 minutes. Our lower temp with longer time compensates for sea-level baking conditions.

reminders.prompt: Rate crust color and oven spring

states.title: Cool on Rack
states.direction: Transfer rolls to a wire rack. Let cool for at least 20 minutes before eating — the crumb is still setting as it cools.
states.exit_condition: Rolls have cooled at least 20 minutes, crust should be audibly crackly when tapped

notes.text: Store in a paper bag with small holes punched throughout — this maintains crustiness. Never plastic. Best eaten same-day, especially for tortas ahogadas.
For tortas ahogadas: split the birote lengthwise, spread with refried beans, fill with carnitas and pickled red onions, then drown in chile de arbol salsa and tomato broth.
Freeze extras in a zip-lock bag. Reheat from frozen at 400°F (200°C) for 8-10 minutes to revive the crust.

techniques.name: Beer/lime/egg levain (Puratos #72 protocol)
techniques.sourcedFrom: Puratos Library, Stellanspice, Breadtopia, Grupo La Florida
techniques.rationale: The only sourdough starter among 133 in the Puratos collection fed with this combination. Creates selection pressure for T. delbrueckii yeast via hops antimicrobial, low pH, and ethanol tolerance.

techniques.name: 62.5% hydration (professional formula)
techniques.rationale: Professional GDL bakery hydration. Lower than home-baker recipes (73-80%+) but produces the dense, sauce-resistant crumb that defines authentic birote.

techniques.name: Oven-off steam method
techniques.rationale: Turn oven off during initial 20-min steam phase. Residual heat allows maximum oven spring without premature crust set. Critical for gas ovens that vent steam.

techniques.name: Dark hi-bake finish
techniques.rationale: Move to top rack for final 3-5 minutes. Authentic birotes are darker than typical sourdough — the thick, hard crust must survive sauce submersion.

techniques.name: Cold levain retard (12-48 hrs)
techniques.rationale: Develops sour tang that altitude-accelerated fermentation produces naturally in Guadalajara. Longer retard = more tang.

techniques.name: Water treatment for Austin
techniques.sourcedFrom: Austin Water Authority data, baking science literature
techniques.rationale: Austin water (pH 8.82, 290 mg/L hardness, chloramine) is too alkaline and hard. Carbon filter + 50/50 dilution with distilled brings closer to Guadalajara's volcanic Na-HCO3 water profile.

research.strategy: 7-agent parallel research: Stellanspice deep dive, sourdough community recipes, Spanish-language sources, sourdough science, torta ahogada context, Reddit/forum replication attempts, water/altitude compensation

methods.detail: 400°F (200°C), 5-8 min. Spritz with water before reheating to revive the shattering crust. From frozen: 8-10 min at 400°F (200°C).
Split lengthwise, spread with refried beans, fill with carnitas and pickled red onions. Drown in chile de arbol salsa and tomato broth. Eat with hands (gloves optional).
Paper bag with pin holes punched throughout — never plastic. Best same-day. Freeze in zip-lock for up to 1 month. Austin humidity will soften the crust faster than in Guadalajara.

cook_log.summary: First bake of birote salado — made 4 rolls instead of 5, shaped more like baguettes than torpedoes due to shaping difficulty. Surprisingly good results with strong sour tang that lingered ~10 minutes after eating.
notes: Levain cold fermented overnight in fridge, pulled out in the morning
Used Modelo Especial for the beer
Used Zero Water filtered water — no 50/50 distilled dilution, never had issues with water
Dough temp after mixing: 74.3°F
Coil fold 1 temp: 75.6°F
Coil fold 2 temp: 78.3°F
Coil fold 3 temp: 78.6°F
Coil fold 4 temp: 79.4°F
Divided into 4 rolls (~230g each) instead of 5 — didn't want to run a full dutch oven steam/cook cycle for one single roll, can only fit 2 at a time
Had trouble getting the torpedo shape — ended up more baguette-shaped, not uniform yet
Forgot to log pre-shape timing and shaping details
Baked in dutch oven in batches of 2. Set uncovered phase timer to 16 min to check at 15. Very good results — strong sour tang that lingered ~10 minutes after eating. Ate the bread by itself.

photos.alt: Two birote rolls baking in a dutch oven on parchment paper during the uncovered browning phase. Rolls show good oven spring with lengthwise scores opened wide.
Two finished birote rolls cooling on a round wire rack. Deep golden-brown to dark crust with heavy flour dusting, lengthwise scores opened cleanly.
Birote roll being dipped into a small bowl of birria consommé on a white plate. Crust shows golden-brown color with flour dusting.
Hand holding a broken birote roll showing open, irregular crumb structure with a mix of large and medium alveoli. Light and airy interior with a thin but defined crust edge.

next_time.text: Find better shaping instructions — ideally a YouTube video with timestamped torpedo technique
Work on getting more uniform, professional-looking shape
